# Double-dummy trick tables from an independent program, as an oracle for the
# solver dealer3 calls.
#
# Source: a BridgeComposer 5.97 hand record for a Common Game session of
# 2026-01-19, whose OptimumResultTable holds all twenty (declarer, strain)
# results per board. BridgeComposer computes these itself, so agreeing with it
# checks dealer3's whole path end to end - the deal conversion, the opening
# leader, and the declarer-versus-North/South trick conversion - against
# something that shares no code with it.
#
# One board per line: the PBN Deal tag, then twenty trick counts, declarer
# N, E, S, W outermost and denomination C, D, H, S, NT within each.
#
# Five lines are marked `quick`. Those are the boards this solver gets through
# fastest - a table costs anywhere from 20ms to 480ms optimised, and fifteen
# times that unoptimised - and they are the ones an unoptimised `cargo test`
# checks. The wiring under test is the same on every board, so which boards a
# debug build spends its time on is only a question of how long it takes.
